title: Explore the orders and pick the report's columns
prompt:
The sales team's daily report starts from the shop's raw order export: the `orders` table below, 3,012 rows straight from the system. Look at it first. Add `orders.printSchema()` and `print(orders.count())` inside `order_view`, before its `return`, and press Run to see its columns and size.

Then write `order_view(orders)`. It returns the columns the report uses, in the report's order, with `total` renamed to `order_total`. Every row stays, even the strange ones: this step only shapes the columns.
rules: `order_total` is `total` under its new name, with the same type and values.
Every row of `orders` is still there, duplicates and odd rows included.
hints: `select` picks columns in the order you list them.
Don't filter yet: the next step decides which rows the report can use.
starter:
